hed: Sualocin: A Bright Beacon in Delphinus
dek: Discover the characteristics and significance of this notable star, also known as Alpha Delphini.
body:
Sualocin, officially designated as Alpha Delphini, is a prominent star located in the constellation Delphinus, the dolphin. Situated at celestial coordinates approximately 20.66 hours of right ascension and 15.91 degrees of declination, Sualocin stands out as a notable figure within its stellar neighborhood. Its brightness and relative accessibility make it a favored target for amateur astronomers and astrophotographers alike. Sualocin's identity is well established as a figure star within the constellation, and it forms an integral part of the recognized asterism known as Job's Coffin.

Physically, Sualocin is classified as a star that belongs to the star family, offering insights into stellar evolution and characteristics. While specific details about its spectral type, luminosity, and distance remain within the realm of astronomers’ ongoing observations, its position within the celestial sphere renders it a key reference point for star charts and navigational purposes.

The star's name, Sualocin, has historical intrigue, often linked to early 19th-century star catalogues and naming conventions adopted by astronomers. It is part of a segment of the sky that has been carefully studied and documented, serving both scientific and cultural functions in our understanding of the universe.

As an accepted figure star and a potential physical object candidate, Sualocin offers valuable opportunities for research, including spectroscopy and astrometry, to better comprehend its physical attributes and role within the constellation. Its stability and brightness contribute to its importance as a fixed point in the night sky, anchoring further discoveries within the celestial tapestry of Delphinus. Observing this star allows both professionals and enthusiasts to appreciate the intricate architecture of our galaxy and deepen our collective understanding of the cosmos.
